nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis of SnO2
nodes.procedure: SnO2 catalyst was synthesized following the previously reported hydrothermal method detailed in reference [21] (P. Sun et al., CrystEngComm 2012, 14, 1701-1708; see Supporting Information for details).
nodes.source_text: The SnO2 catalyst was synthesized following the previously reported hydrothermal method (see Supporting Information for details).

nodes.description: Ethylene electrooxidation to 2-chloroethanol at 100 mA/cm² with different chloride concentrations (highest FE in 2 M NaCl)
nodes.source_text: ethylene electrooxidation tests were conducted under different Cl⁻ concentrations at a constant current density of 100mAcm⁻²... with the highest FE of 85% for 2-chloroethanol and 13% for residue active chlorine species in 2MNaCl solution... among the 85% FE of 2-chloroethanol, 7% results from the CER pathway and 78% originates from the new pathway. Thus, the selectivity of the new pathway accounts for 92% of total 2-chloroethanol.

nodes.description: Ethylene electrooxidation stability test at 100 mA/cm² in 2 M NaCl for 50 h
nodes.source_text: The stability of the SnO₂ catalyst was assessed at the current density of 100mAcm⁻². Within a duration of 50h, the system maintained a stable applied potential of 2.0(±0.05)V and an average FE of 82% (Figure 3c).

nodes.description: LSV polarization curves in NaCl vs Na₂SO₄

electrolyte.value: 2 M NaCl or Na₂SO₄ with saturated C₂H₄

nodes.source_text: linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) polarization curves of SnO₂ in 2MNaCl or Na₂SO₄ solutions with saturated C₂H₄ were collected (Figure 3d). A sharp increase in anodic current began at 1.35V vs. SHE in NaCl electrolyte

nodes.description: LSV comparison with N₂ vs C₂H₄ in 2 M NaCl
nodes.source_text: comparison with the LSV curve under nitrogen (N₂) atmosphere shows that reaction under C₂H₄ gave rise to a considerably increased response current (Figure 3e)

nodes.description: Tafel slope analysis for chlorine-participated ethylene oxidation vs CER
nodes.source_text: The Tafel slope of reactions under C₂H₄ and N₂ atmospheres is measured to be 169.59 and 341.52mVdec⁻¹, respectively (Figure 4b)

nodes.description: Faradaic efficiency of 2-chloroethanol at different current densities in 2 M NaCl
nodes.source_text: Impressively, negligible change in FEs of 2-chloroethanol was observed at the current density ranging from 50 to 250mAcm⁻² in 2MNaCl (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD indicates pure SnO2 phase with no impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) indicated that a pure SnO2 product was obtained (Figures S1 and S2).
The X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) indicated that a pure SnO2 product was obtained (Figures S1 and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: SnO2 particles were of urchin-like morphology with a rather uniform size of around 1 μm in diameter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that SnO2 particles were of urchin-like morphology with a rather uniform size of around 1μm in diameter (Figures 2a and S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: SnO2 particles were of urchin-like morphology with a rather uniform size of around 1 μm in diameter.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that SnO2 particles were of urchin-like morphology with a rather uniform size of around 1μm in diameter (Figures 2a and S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: High crystallinity with exposed SnO2 (110) surface, lattice spacing of 3.34 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image further highlighted their high crystallinity with the exposed SnO2 (110) surface, characterized by the lattice spacing of 3.34Å (Figure 2b).

Scanning Electron Microscopy image showing nanostructured material with flower-like morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Sn K-edge XAFS spectra exhibit similar features to commercial SnO2 but with slightly decreased amplitude.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectra of SnO2 catalyst at the Sn K-edge exhibit similar features to the commercial SnO2, but with slightly decreased amplitude (Figures S4 and S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows reduced Sn-O coordination number of CN = 5.6 (vs. 6 in bulk), indicating unsaturated Sn sites on particle surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier-transformed extended Xray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) analysis reveals a reduced coordination number (CN = 5.6) in the first Sn-O scattering shell, lower than the saturated value (CN = 6) from SnO2 crystallographic model (Figures S6 and S7; Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peaks at 472 cm⁻¹ (Eg), 632 cm⁻¹ (A1g), and 774 cm⁻¹ (B2g) confirm SnO2 vibrational modes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman peaks at 472, 632, and 774 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the Eg, A1g, and B2g vibrational modes of as-prepared SnO2, respectively (Figure S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows *Cl peak at 502 cm⁻¹ (intensity varies with potential) and *OH peak at 579 cm⁻¹ (red shifts to 561 cm⁻¹ with H₂¹⁸O isotope labeling) on SnO2 surface during ethylene oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ Raman spectrum recorded in ethylene-saturated NaCl aqueous solution displays that two new peaks emerge at 502 and 579 cm⁻¹, respectively (Figure 2f).
